help.polling:
Connect Slack, checking for messages

1. api.slack.com/apps › Create New App › From scratch. Name it Munder Difflin and pick your workspace.
2. OAuth & Permissions › Bot Token Scopes: add channels:history, groups:history, chat:write and files:read. Install to workspace.
3. Copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb) into the Bot token field here, and the channel id into Channel.
4. Invite the bot to that channel: /invite @MunderDifflin
5. Press Test connection, then Turn on. No Event Subscriptions, no Request URL.
help.socket:
Connect Slack, staying connected

1. api.slack.com/apps › Create New App › From scratch. Name it Munder Difflin and pick your workspace.
2. OAuth & Permissions › Bot Token Scopes: add channels:history, groups:history, chat:write and files:read. Install to workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb) into Bot token here.
3. Socket Mode › Enable Socket Mode. Basic Information › App Level Tokens › Generate, scope connections:write. Copy the token (xapp) into App token here.
4. Event Subscriptions › Enable Events › Subscribe to bot events: add message.channels and message.groups. No Request URL is needed. Save, reinstall if Slack asks.
5. Invite the bot to the channel: /invite @MunderDifflin, put the channel id in Channel, press Test connection, then Turn on.
help.webhook:
Connect Slack, letting Slack call the office

1. api.slack.com/apps › Create New App › From scratch. Name it Munder Difflin and pick your workspace.
2. Basic Information › Signing Secret: copy it into the Signing secret field here.
3. OAuth & Permissions › Bot Token Scopes: add chat:write, channels:history and groups:history. Install to workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb) into the Bot token field here.
4. Press start below to launch the webhook and get your Request URL.
5. Event Subscriptions › Enable Events › Request URL: paste the Request URL from here and wait for Slack's green check.
6. Event Subscriptions › Subscribe to bot events: add message.channels and message.groups.
7. Event Subscriptions › Subscribe to events on behalf of users (add the matching user token scopes channels:history and groups:history first if Slack asks): add message.channels and message.groups.
8. Save Changes, reinstall if Slack prompts, then invite the bot to your channel: /invite @MunderDifflin

The Request URL changes on every start, so paste it again after a restart.

permissions.autoLabelPlain: LET AGENTS WORK ON THEIR OWN
permissions.autoOnPlain: On. Agents carry out tasks without stopping to ask — the smoothest experience.

permissions.reliabilityHead: KEEP THINGS RUNNING WHILE YOU'RE AWAY
permissions.reliabilityDescPlain: Your agents keep working on a schedule and in live terminals, even when you step away. These settings keep you in the loop and keep things running.
permissions.reliabilityDesc: Your agents keep working on a schedule and in live terminals. If your computer fully sleeps those timers pause and catch up the moment you're back — nothing is lost, it may just run late.
permissions.keepAwakeDesc: Strong keep-alive: stops your computer from sleeping while an agent is live, so schedules and terminals fire on time even when you step away. Uses more battery — best on power. Off by default.
permissions.notificationsDesc: Get pinged when an agent needs you or a terminal needs reviving — even while you're away. Your system may ask permission the first time one fires.
permissions.openAtLoginDesc: Relaunch the harness after a reboot so scheduled missions resume on their own. No prompt — applies immediately.
permissions.shareStatsDesc: A handful of anonymous events (app opened, agent spawned, feature used) that help improve Munder Difflin — never prompts, code, file paths, or agent output. Full list in TELEMETRY.md; change anytime in Settings.
permissions.stayAwakeDescMac: macOS only lets you set this one yourself. In Battery → Options, turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off" (on power adapter) so timers keep firing with the display asleep. Without a sleep-preventing setting the Mac still truly sleeps — work survives and catches up on wake.
permissions.stayAwakeDescWindows: Windows only lets you set this one yourself. In Settings → System → Power & battery → Screen, blank & sleep, set "On battery power, put my device to sleep" and "When plugged in" to Never (or increase them) so timers keep firing. Without a sleep-preventing setting Windows still truly sleeps — work survives and catches up on wake.
permissions.stayAwakeDescLinux: Your desktop environment only lets you set this one yourself. Look for a Power Settings panel (e.g. GNOME Settings → Power, or KDE System Settings → Power Management) and disable automatic sleep/suspend while on power. Without a sleep-preventing setting your machine still truly sleeps — work survives and catches up on wake.
permissions.teamNote: You chose this when you joined. Change it any time in Triggers, under Network.

authWhy.none: Nothing is added to the request. For an API that needs no key.
authWhy.bearer: Sends Authorization: Bearer and your key. The most common shape; Stripe, Notion and Sentry use it.
authWhy.header: Sends your key on its own under a header you name. Pick this when the docs show a header with no word in front of the key.
authWhy.prefix: Sends a word and then your key under a header you name. Pick this when the docs show Token, ApiKey or SSWS in front of it.
authWhy.query: Sends your key as a query parameter on every URL. Common on weather, news and maps APIs.
authWhy.basic: Sends a user and your key as HTTP basic. Atlassian, Twilio and Mailgun take an email and a token this way.
authWhy.github: Sends Authorization: Bearer and your token, with the two headers the GitHub REST API expects.

conn.headerHint: The header name from your provider's docs. Letters, digits and hyphens.
conn.prefixHint: One word. The space before your key is added for you.
conn.paramHint: The parameter name from your provider's docs.
conn.userHint: The left half of the pair, usually an email. Your key is the right half and stays in the encrypted store.
conn.sendsNothing: Nothing is added to the request.
conn.sendsMasked: The stars stand where your key goes. The key itself is never shown again.
conn.errPrefix: The prefix is one word of letters, digits or hyphens.
conn.errParam: The parameter name may hold letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens only.
conn.errUser: Give the user for the pair, without a colon.
conn.errDuplicate: A connection already uses that id. Change the label.

orchestrator.name: The orchestrator

temps.name: Temps
